summary: MODIS and VIIRS data from NASA FIRMS, applied across all of Argentina from 2000 to 2026. Our team, rather than comparing isolated points, our team groups hotspots into physically meaningful units: fires, which cluster touching pixels within a 12-hour window, and firewaves, which link fires across multiple days. Each unit includes its own polygon as well as a confidence score that combines both sensors. This is our proposed harmonisation. In this way, the source sensor no longer matters, just as the challenge requires. Because the method uses the actual size of each pixel, it adapts seamlessly to new satellites once MODIS is decommissioned. We also included a pilot test in Córdoba—the province from which CONAE launched the challenge—featuring a CNN + LSTM model that forecasts new hotspots seven days ahead. Furthermore, the web application -Mente Fría- provides a space for firefighters to log field reports in each hotspot's activity log, which could help guide future action plans. This work matters because wildfires are becoming increasingly frequent and intense, meaning emergency managers need a reliable historical reference.
details:
mente fría is a web tool with a harmonized fire activity calendar for Argentina (2000 to 2026), built from the MODIS and VIIRS hotspots of NASA FIRMS, plus a pilot that predicts new hotspots seven days ahead in Córdoba.

What it does and how it works
MODIS and VIIRS records cannot be compared directly because they differ in pixel size, confidence scale and observation times. Instead of comparing isolated points, we group about 6.4 million hotspots into physically meaningful units. A fire is a cluster of hotspots whose pixels touch within the same 12-hour window. Each pixel is approximated by a circle whose radius is half its real diagonal (scan and track from FIRMS), so the same rule works for MODIS-MODIS, VIIRS-VIIRS and mixed pairs. A firewave chains fires over time using the NASA FEDS approach (1 km buffer, 5 km in forested protected areas, 5-day window). The result is about 1.95 million fires and 1.19 million firewaves, each with its own polygon and a confidence metric that combines both sensors, counts independent overpasses instead of points and is comparable across eras. MODIS confidence is mapped to the VIIRS classes with NASA's official thresholds, and each fire records whether it occurred in a protected area or in forest (NASA MCD12Q1).
The mente fría web app lets users pick a region (country, 24 provinces or 529 departments) and a period on a timeline by days, weeks or months. The map shows fire polygons colored by confidence or the raw hotspots by sensor, and highlights the whole firewave of a selected fire. The calendar shows daily burning area and number of fires, with the area harmonized to the VIIRS scale, and eight fire seasons week by week. Firefighters can write reports linked to a firewave, building a field log next to the satellite data.
For Córdoba, a CNN + LSTM model trained on 2019 to 2025 data uses 14 days of hotspot history, NASA POWER weather, land cover and protected areas to predict hotspots for the next seven days, using the Open-Meteo forecast in operation. Predicted hotspots are grouped into fires and firewaves with the same rules, and the app shows them in yellow with a clear warning that they are estimates. On the test period the model reaches a ROC-AUC of 0.84 and a recall of 0.67 at a 0.5 threshold, outperforming persistence and climatology baselines.

Benefits
A fire activity series comparable across 26 years, where the change of sensors or the number of satellites no longer distorts the result. Units that represent real fires instead of pixels, with polygons, duration and transparent confidence. Environmental context to prioritize sensitive areas. A method that keeps working without MODIS and adds new VIIRS satellites through configuration only. Open outputs in Parquet and GeoPackage.

Intended impact
Give early warning teams, firefighters, land managers and researchers a consistent historical reference to identify critical months and years, detect anomalies and prioritize monitoring. Turn each field intervention into accumulated knowledge through the firefighter log, which could later support action plans. Show how the same harmonized base can move from describing the past to anticipating the coming days.

Tools
Python (DuckDB, pandas, GeoPandas, Shapely, PyProj, SciPy, scikit-learn, rasterio, PyArrow) for the harmonization pipeline. PyTorch for the CNN + LSTM model, trained on an NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU. TypeScript, Next.js, React and MapLibre GL for the web app. QGIS for visual validation. Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS), NASA POWER, NASA MCD12Q1, Open-Meteo, NOAA ONI and IGN Argentina boundaries and protected areas. Generative AI: we used Claude (Anthropic), through Claude Code, as a coding and writing assistant for the web app, the prediction model, the data processing scripts, the documentation and the video editing. The team defined the method, reviewed every output and validated the results.

Creativity
We compare fires instead of points, using a contact rule based on the real size of each pixel. The confidence metric does not reward the larger number of satellites of recent years. The prediction stays consistent with the harmonization because the model predicts hotspots and then applies the same fire and firewave definitions. Satellite data and firefighters' field experience live in the same tool.

Factors considered
Sensor differences in resolution, confidence and timing. Comparability across eras (from one to five satellites). The end of MODIS, the Terra standby, the end of S-NPP and future VIIRS satellites. Near real-time data without the type field, inferred from the archive. Border fires, grouped before clipping to Argentina. Data licenses (we used the official IGN protected areas instead of WDPA). Information leakage in the prediction, avoided with time-split periods and a seven-day purge. Clear communication of estimates: predicted data uses a separate yellow scale and hides the model score, which is always 80 % or more because only cells above the 0.8 threshold are exported.
